correctness.rationale: The rooted-plane-tree DFS encoding gives P=L and D=2(H-n) pointwise. Slot counting establishes all conditional means and E[L H] including the leaf-depth auxiliary W. Induction proves E[L]=(2n+1)/3 and E[W]=(2/3)E[H]+(n+2)/9; subtraction yields c_1=0, c_{n+1}=(2n+2)/(2n+1)c_n-2/9. The rational closed solution and sign follow by substitution and induction; the limit follows from the central-binomial estimate. An exact independent tree decoder checks 146599 words; 1069 conditional insertion cases are exhaustively checked for sizes through five. No finite check substitutes for the induction.

originality.rationale: The new exact mixed covariance of local plateau count and global summed nesting span has a recurrence and strict all-order sign not stated in inspected prior papers. Janson gives the contour correspondence and plateau marginals, Kuba–Panholzer gives individual label-spacing laws, and Lundblad–Wagner gives a broad PDE encoding leaf-count/path-length moments but proves different normalized path-length comparisons. That PDE implicitly contains mixed moments and is the principal residual priority risk; its presence is fully acknowledged, not treated as a failed search.
residual_risks: The 2026 multivariate generating-function equation encodes joint leaf/path-length moments and could yield this mixed covariance after unreported differentiation and coefficient extraction; exact historical priority requires specialist comparison of possible hidden derivations.
General statistics of increasing trees in older monographs and unpublished earlier preprints may have an equivalent explicit formula under different variables.
The claim is an exact finite mixed moment and sign theorem, not a general result for all preferential-attachment parameters.

value.rationale: Leaf/plateau abundance is a natural local terminal statistic; the total nesting span is the natural sum of all internal interval widths, equivalently the total path length of the associated increasing tree. Their exact mixed covariance links two separately studied observables, yields strict negative dependence for every nontrivial order, and has the precise linear-scale coefficient -8/9. Neither marginal distribution alone supplies the result; it is not an arbitrary small finite table.
